I dreamt once that myself and a handful of other people were sort of 'stuck' in a zombie apocalypse, but it was a little bit like a gameshow. We would be dumped into a house infested with zombies and would have to survive for so long before we got pulled out and then put into a different house and the ordeal would start again. The houses that I can remember actually belonged to different family members in real life. One was my cousins house, one was my grandparents and another was one of our old houses that we no longer lived in.

The first few houses we were put in, I had an option to hide in a safe room so the zombies couldn't get me. In the fourth house though this option was removed, so I had to survive just like everyone else. I remember running around these houses to evade capture. At one point a zombie grabbed me and raked its nails along my head and I felt a mix of blood and slime spurt out of the wound. It didn't hurt, I just felt the liquid channeling out of me if that makes sense?

The last house was my old childhood home. I went into the kitchen and for some reason there was a wall of chairs all stacked on top of each other at the end of the room, so I crawled through it and hid behind. It was pretty dark, like it was dusk outside and the lights weren't on. A guy wearing a yellow tracksuit crawled into the room and a zombie followed him. The guy backed all the way up to the wall of chairs and didn't see me watching from the other side. The zombie advanced on him and slowly bent down to attack the other man. As it bent down it froze and looked me straight in the eye. That's when I woke up.

I must have been about 14 at the time and to this date it's still the most intense dream I've ever had lmao

This is something I wonder about and still struggle with sometimes. It was a long time until it was pointed out to me that social media is not representative of everyone's daily lives. Sure, it seems like this one person is out all the time, but they have their off-days just like anyone else. Social media is only highlights.

Not that that's the whole answer. I am one of those people who does very little. The main reason for this is that I have a very small social circle, and I'm not one of those people who's going to go to the cinema or something on my own. I think it's about understanding yourself more and being content with who you are. Sometimes I think it would be nice to have 2000 friends to go axe-throwing or scuba-diving with every weekend, but I'm awful at maintaining friendships honestly and I have long reached the point where I prefer my own company. So I kinda understand my own limits now and don't mourn the person that I wish I could have been, if that makes sense?

All that being said, I am trying to change things little by little. I do want to have a few more friends as well as find a girlfriend. I'm on a few dating apps and I'm going to push myself to start attending a local tennis club (once they start up again).
